youtubeTitle: She started with 3 cows and limited market access. A year later, she'd earned Rs 11.5 lakh.
caption:
She started with 3 cows and limited market access. A year later, she'd earned Rs 11.5 lakh.

Kaushalya Devi, from Barhi village in Chauri Chaura, Gorakhpur district, Uttar Pradesh, joined the Shri Baba Gorakhnath Kripa Milk Producer Organisation - a women-led dairy cooperative under the National Rural Livelihood Mission - starting with just 3 cows. She now owns 14 cattle, supplies around 70 litres of milk daily and earned roughly Rs 11.5 lakh in her first year, growing to nearly Rs 14 lakh within 18 months - recognized as a 'Lakhpati Didi.' She also installed a home biogas unit, cutting her LPG dependency. She shared her story with UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and was personally acknowledged by PM Modi at the UP International Trade Show in Greater Noida. Her cooperative now has roughly 31,000 women members across four districts, with Rs 93 crore paid directly to women.
